Measure a representative XML unit with CPU utilization, memory and I/O counters. Compare 1, 4 and 8 workers within the 32-core allocation before scaling. Use a CPU budget of 8 cores initially and cap memory and concurrent I/O. Split only at valid record boundaries. Keep serial execution if measured storage limits explain it.
Write atomic checkpoint outputs, validate completed units and resume unfinished units after interruption. Build a persistent index keyed by snapshot fingerprint and relevant config, reuse it for downstream selections, and invalidate it when either changes. Stream chunks rather than holding the XML in memory.
